title: 1977 AHSME Problem 6
statement: If \(x,\) \(y\) and \(2x+\frac y2\) are not zero, then \[ \left(2x+\frac y2\right)^{-1}\left[(2x)^{-1}+\left(\frac y2\right)^{-1}\right] \] equals

solutions.text:
We have \[ \begin{aligned} \left(2x+\frac y2\right)^{-1} &=\frac2{4x+y},\\ (2x)^{-1}+\left(\frac y2\right)^{-1} &=\frac1{2x}+\frac2y\\ &=\frac{y+4x}{2xy}. \end{aligned} \] Their product is \(\frac{1}{xy}=(xy)^{-1}.\)

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Rewrite the outside reciprocal using a single fraction
Combine the two reciprocals inside the brackets over a common denominator
